audit.whatIsWrong: Bloodlust is never named in either layer, yet both layers are built around anti-heal ('Anti-heal his crits', 'Anti-heal his crit healing', 'his healing fights your pattern').
audit.why: Tryndamere's healing is Bloodlust (Q), a 12-second, zero-cost button that converts banked Fury into health, and the same ability passively raises his Attack Damage the more wounded he is. Calling it 'crit healing' points the player at the wrong mechanic: there is no lifesteal on his crits to cut, there is a heal button on a countable 12s timer that must be pre-empted with Grievous Wounds. The 'more wounded, more AD' half is also missing, and it is the reason a half-finished all-in is worse than no all-in.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust (Q), 12s, no cost: spends Fury to heal, and his AD rises as his health falls. Grievous Wounds must land before your burst, not during it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json — Q Bloodlust, cd 12, cost 0, heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early: 'His Mocking Shout slows you and shaves your AD if you face away'.
audit.why: The conditional is attached to the wrong half. Mocking Shout reduces the Attack Damage of every nearby champion unconditionally; only the Move Speed reduction requires the target's back to be turned. As written the line implies you can dodge both effects by facing him, when in fact facing him dodges exactly one — and that one is the half that decides whether Spinning Slash catches you. Retreating while facing Tryndamere is a real, concrete micro-play and the entry currently hides it.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout (W), 14s, 850 range: cuts your AD whether you face him or not; it only slows you if your back is turned. Walk out facing him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json — W Mocking Shout: 'decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.'

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and the dos/donts track only Undying Rage, described as 'Unkillable 5s' with no cooldown, and the punishable window is never named.
audit.why: Every Tryndamere ability costs zero resource, so there is no mana window to wait for — the only timers that exist are cooldowns, which makes stating them the entire game. Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1. The window that actually decides lane trades is Spinning Slash at 12s at rank 1: it is simultaneously his gap-close and his only exit, so the twelve seconds after he spends it are when Ambessa's dash chain can stick. That sequence appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage 120s at rank 1; Spinning Slash 12s at rank 1 and free — it is both his engage and his escape, so commit inside the 12s after he spends it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json — R 120/100/80, E 12/11/10/9/8 cost 0, Q/W/E/R all cost 0

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[1].why: 'Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade.' Ambessa's passive grants no shield.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step gives a dash, an empowered next attack and an energy refund. The shield is Repudiation (W), and against a crit auto-attacker it is the strongest button in her kit for a reason the entry never states: damage she blocks during the brace amplifies the slam. Tryndamere's crit autos and Spinning Slash are exactly the non-minion damage that feeds it.
audit.corrected: Repudiation (W), 18/17/16/15/14: brace his crit autos, and the blocked damage amplifies the slam you fire back.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — P Drakehound's Step (no shield), W Repudiation
